Working on alignment from head to toe is one of the key concepts behind MTF program. 

Our mischievous little one worked really hard during his intensive where we did series of Dynamic Flex Casts to get better alignment, CIMT and long hip cast to reduce the risk of subluxation and help with better posture and muscle activation. 

Cant wait to see him get stronger and stronger!

#mtfprogram #physicaltherapy #hemiplegia

Better alignment begins with better muscle activation!

Here our little one with SMA had excessive lumbar lordosis and poor trunk control due to poor muscle activation. We used  NISE-Stim® which helps facilitate activation of key postural muscles. This inturn improved his trunk stability and more efficient movement pattern . When combined with appropriate therapy methods, this can lead to lasting improvements in alignment and motor control.

The upcoming NISE-Stim Course in India 🇮🇳is scheduled for January 2027. For additional information, please visit website at spinalstim.net or feel free to DM with any questions you may have.

#sma #pediatrictherapy #nisestim #posture

Having a correct alignment while moving is crucial for a better muscle activation and then to strengthen the neural connections.  Here our little one was having difficulty with turning the arm (unable to supinate the forearm) which was limiting his functions so we started with a simple tool of rotahugger by @ferrerpediatrics and simple toy to start activating the right muscle where we saw an instant change in movements and the next day he could activate the muscles even better. 

 #physicaltherapy #mtfprogram #rotahugger #hemiplegia #cerebralpalsy

Posture is a reflection of how the nervous system has learned to control the body, not simply a matter of trying harder.

Long-term changes happen when the brain repeatedly experiences better muscle activation and alignment during meaningful movement. Here we used a valuable technique NISE-Stim® which  provides consistent neuromuscular input, and helps reinforce more efficient postural patterns while children continue to engage in functional activities.

The upcoming in-person course in India 🇮🇳 is in January 2027. To register visit spinalstim.net

Small victories are so important!
We're using NISE-Stim by @nisestimtherapy to help our little one with involuntary painful movements in her trunk and hips. After following a tone modulation protocol tailored for our warrior, we saw better hip positioning and fewer involuntary movements. This then helped us with developmental positions and motor control, which was tough before the tone modulation.

#cerebralpalsy #dystonia #quadriplegic

Moving from quadruped to sitting isn't just about changing positions, it's about building the foundation for functional movement.

In this activity, we:
🔹 Start in quadruped with one leg extended
🔹 Use a motivating toy on the opposite side to encourage reaching and rotation
🔹 Facilitate a gentle weight shift through the pelvis
🔹 Guide the movement just enough for the child to actively find their way into sitting

Why is this important for children with spastic diplegia?

✅ Improves pelvic mobility
✅ Encourages hip opening and dissociation
✅ Develops weight-shifting skills
✅ Strengthens trunk control
✅ Promotes active movement rather than relying on compensation patterns

These transitions help children learn how to move efficiently between positions, an essential skill for play, exploration, and independence.

Sometimes the biggest gains come from practicing the movements in between milestones. 💛

Physical activity and exercise can be highly effective in treating back pain and are recommended as the first-line of treatment before considering opioids or surgery. 🏋️‍♀️💪 However, the use of opioid prescriptions for back pain prior to surgery has become increasingly common, with a rate almost 3 times higher than that of physical therapy (84.4% vs 34.1%). This trend is concerning given that opioid use can lead to chronic opioid dependence and abuse following surgery. 🚫💊 This highlights the importance of avoiding opioids whenever possible and instead utilizing exercise and physical therapy as safe and effective alternatives for treating back pain.

Additionally, the use of opioids before surgery is strongly associated with worse patient outcomes, such as pain, function, and quality of life, one year after spine surgery. Furthermore, preoperative opioid use predicts an increased risk of postoperative chronic opioid dependence and abuse. ⚠️🩺

Therefore, clinicians and patients should be aware that prior opioid use can reduce the effectiveness of surgery in reducing opioid dependence. Current best-practice guidelines recommend using other treatments, such as exercise and physical therapy, before considering opioid prescriptions. The high utilization of opioids and low utilization of exercise or physical therapy suggest that current practice patterns are not optimal for achieving the best outcomes. 📈

By prioritizing physical activity and exercise, patients can achieve optimal outcomes and avoid the risks associated with opioid use. 🙌🏃‍♀️

Did you know that getting physical therapy within a month of experiencing lower back pain can reduce the need for surgery by 38%? 🤯 Despite the growing evidence that exercise therapy can help manage lower back pain, studies show that only 16%-38% of patients with musculoskeletal spine disorders are referred to physical therapy. 😔

It's concerning that low use of physical therapy services may be due to patients and clinicians undervaluing the benefits of exercise therapy. Some patients may even believe that exercise could be harmful! 🤔

For effective treatment, physical therapy programs for chronic lower back pain usually require at least 5 weeks of treatment. High-dose programs tend to have better outcomes than low-dose exercise programs. 💪

Sadly, almost three times as many patients receive opioid prescriptions for back pain compared to those who receive physical therapy. While opioids are a popular treatment for back pain before surgery, studies show that they are not better than non-opioid medications. Using opioids before surgery can even predict worse outcomes such as more pain, worse function, and lower quality of life a year after spine surgery. It can even lead to chronic opioid dependence and abuse. 😱

That's why guidelines for best-practice care don't recommend using opioids until other treatments, including exercise and physical therapy, have been tried and failed. 💊

recent_reviews.text: The macarons were delightful. Light, airy, and flavorful. The lemon tart was perfect. The crust was buttery and flakey. The filling was thick and full of lemon flavor. The brownie with walnut was exceptional. It was just the way I love my brownies: full of chocolate flavor but not over powering with sugar. The batter was very moist with a nice crust. The walnuts were and big and a nice flavor compliment to the cocoa. Great customer service. I was glad I ran to make it to your store before you closed for the night.

recent_reviews.text: So pretty. The customer service was excellent. The ice cream was other worldly.

recent_reviews.text: We ordered a small lemon cake for our elopement dinner. Ordering ahead of time online was super simple, which I appreciated since we were out of state. I couldn't help but buy more goodies and sweets when we went into the shop to pick up the cake!  The cake was just lovely, macaroons were amazing, and we're still nibbling on the English toffee now that we're back home. Thank you, Miette, for making our elopement and trip a sweet one!

reviews.text: This was my first time at this shopping complex and this store and my experience was very disappointing. I was met with silence upon entering the store and even going up to the register was not even given a hello nor offered any type of help or support (keep in mind I was the only customer there). They just rung me up and didn’t bother to ask if I needed anything else. I’m not sure if it is because I do not look like the usual clientele at this store or not but it was disheartening to not be acknowledged or even looked at.

A variety of delights similar to Ferry Building but do have limitations on availability due to lower supply on Macaroons. A smaller store makes for tight spot if more that 2-3 people but good for pick up to go will swing by if in area and hope they have the flavor of Macaroons I look for
I had an amazing time at Miette! The candy options were great, and the worker Sophie was really helpful with pricing and other questions I had!
Great cookies
Love the treats here but they are randomly closed and aren't actually open during normal business hours. Call first.
Tiny little patisserie that also has a small range of candy. I like the cookies - gingersnaps and graham crackers, specifically - and the Turkish Delight.

I was rather disappointed by the cake that I picked up for my birthday. 1st of all they forgot to put the writing on the cake. 2nd of all the cake was dry and the frosting was crumbling off the cake. I've had this cake before and it was delicious so I'm not quite sure what went wrong this time.

I ordered the Buche de Noel! It is absolutely perfection. Beautiful and equally delicious. The sponge is light and airy, the filling fluffy and the ganache is decadent. Joanne provided excellent customer service.

Well I’m beaming today fish family! This is truly an iconic SF weekend! SF CRAB is open at last and boy, they are just gorgeous! Averaging 1.75-2 lbs each. Add to that, the 49ers are gonna push past the Packers as we all watch with big smiles feasting all the while on our favorite local delicacy! 🦀>🧀

HAVE A PARTY Y’ALL! Pick crab, shuck oysters, make poke bowls, snack on the finest salmon sashimi with your friends and family. This special weekend has been a long time coming! ENJOY! 

Big shouts to all the extremely hard-working folks out on the water and on the docks and my team, working feverishly to bring you all the very best!
McFARLAND SPRINGS CA NATIVE RAINBOW TROUT           Cold smoked (lox)
The most local tuna in town. ALBACORE ~ Fatty, oily, rich, delicious ~ Monterey Bay Aquarium’s Seafood Watch 💚Best Choice💚 USA troll caught, 0 bycatch
Grateful for my passionate, dedicated, thoughtful, sustainability minded, local partners who produce the most delightful morsels and items.
https://abnb.me/RlLAgROOQub I got a hankering to get back on the pier to share my passion and perspective with you! Yes there will be sea treats. Hope you can join a trip soon!

Guys, my all time favorite fish is coming in tonight - Day boat albacore tuna (troll caught, Ft. Bragg, Captain Danny Speirn) There is nothing like fresh, day boat albacore. The meat is so clean, tender, and beautiful. Day boat albacore makes some of the best poke, tataki, sashimi, sushi, pan seared fish you will ever eat. 

I am only able to offer FRESH day boat albacore a few times a year, if at all. Albacore are many miles off the coast so most boats fish for a number of days and either bring in frozen fish or fish that is a few days old. Albacore are plentiful, but getting day boat fish is truly exceptional. Danny is heading straight out and then right back in to hook us up with the absolute freshest albacore possible. DO NOT MISS OUT

Did I mention these troll caught California albacore are on the Monterrey bay aquarium’s seafood watch best choice list?

New! Fresh splendid iridescent seaweed salad. Big thanks to Ian @seaquoia_  for harvesting this beautiful local product. This seaweed is tender yet crunchy and damn delicious with all the organic produce and vinegar/sesame dressing mixed in❤️🙏🏼

New seaweed salad on deck! Featuring fresh local dwarf rockweed seaweed from our new friends at @seaquoia_ Stoked to bring you another unique and sustainable dish from the sea❤️🌿🌊 All organic produce of course! Enjoy!                   The second photo is the highly processed, frozen, Chinese imported seaweed salad you find everywhere else.

“We as a nation must undergo a radical revolution of values. We must rapidly begin the shift from a “thing‐oriented” society to a “person‐oriented” society. When machines and computers, profit motives and property rights are considered more important than people, the giant triplets of racism, materialism, and militarism are incapable of being conquered…—MLK jr.                                        Where do we even begin to undergo a revolution of values? With ourselves, our communities, and our businesses. Every week I’m stoked to offer my community a high quality selection of sustainable and traceable seafood. Profits do not come first. Values do. Our seafood selection is small because we are unwilling to sell seafood that comes from places and businesses that do not share our values and standards. Are you ready to revolutionize your values? ✊❤️ Trap caught black cod from fishing vessel Pacific bully, San Francisco.

Add to that, the 49ers are gonna push past the Packers as we all watch with big smiles feasting all the while on our favorite local delicacy! 🦀>🧀

Guys, my all time favorite fish is coming in tonight - Day boat albacore tuna (troll caught, Ft. Bragg, Captain Danny Speirn) There is nothing like fresh, day boat albacore. The meat is so clean, tender, and beautiful. Day boat albacore makes some of the best poke, tataki, sashimi, sushi, pan seared fish you will ever eat. 

I am only able to offer FRESH day boat albacore a few times a year, if at all. Albacore are many miles off the coast so most boats fish for a number of days and either bring in frozen fish or fish that is a few days old. Albacore are plentiful, but getting day boat fish is truly exceptional. Danny is heading straight out and then right back in to hook us up with the absolute freshest albacore possible. DO NOT MISS OUT

Did I mention these troll caught California albacore are on the Monterrey bay aquarium’s seafood watch best choice list?

recent_reviews.text: Unbelievably fresh seafood ! This vendor has been my go-to supplier since the early days of the pandemic . The quality of the fish plus the extraordinary high level of customer service mean that I will be a loyal customer as long as Fishmonger Don is there ! Our world is filled with so much bureaucratic frustration and incompetence that it is amazing to discover Don and his ability to go above and beyond for his clientele . Unparalleled service ! Try it , you'll like it !
recent_reviews.author: Jane J.

recent_reviews.text:
Fishmonger Don has the most amazing, delicious, freshest seafood you will ever be able to purchase as a consumer.  We started ordering from Don in 2020 during the pandemic, and continue to do so each and every week. 
Once you taste his seafood, you will never be able to eat store bought fish again. There is no comparison. 
My son-in-law, who is an avid weekend fisherman on the East Coast, marveled at the size, texture, and flavor of the miso marinated cod we served him last week while visiting. 
We have enjoyed, cod, salmon, gulf shrimp, ahi tuna, trout, uni, scallops, and cioppino from Don. It's all amazing. It's all so good.
recent_reviews.author: Suzanne F.

recent_reviews.text: excellent choice of sustainable fish and sensitivity to environmental concerns is reflected in all the information and packaging. I particularly love the miso sablefish.  Delivery makes this so easy if you're not near a pick up area.

recent_reviews.text: Best sustainable fish available. You definitely get what you pay for! Highly recommended!

recent_reviews.text: Amazing, amazing, amazing!! Fishmonger Don has changed my life! We order fresh from him almost every week and it is incredibly fresh and delicious. The miso cod is our favorite. If you haven't tried it yet, you are missing out!
recent_reviews.author: Rachel P.

recent_reviews.text: This is the BEST fresh fish. We have been buying fish from Don since the very beginning and I would not go anywhere else for our fish. The salmon is a must every week. The crab, oysters, mussels are excellent. The service is always outstanding. Don is always there to answer questions.
recent_reviews.author: Leigha D.

recent_reviews.text: It's really challenging to write this ... because I don't want to let out the secret to the BEST fish in the Bay Area. Fishmonger Don is the real deal. His fish is just amazing and I find it hard to eat any other sourced fish, unless it's just been caught. The service of delivery to my door is a huge added benefit. The miso cod is better than you know whose :). You can't go wrong with anything on the list!

I recently found out that not all interpreters are certified. It varies depending on state. However, we are well within our rights to request for someone who is certified on specific calls. That information does not have to be disclosed either. A few times I called, I asked if they were certified, they gave me puzzled and judgmental looks. One even said she did not have to answer that.

Know your rights. They need to teach all their workers that if Deaf call and request for a certified interpreter, they should have a right to someone certified and not be judged according to their preference. The employees shouldn't even question it at all.
"I need a certified interpreter for this call." Boom. They should find one that is certified or tell you if they are immediately, no questions asked.
Soren.

recent_posts.text: New in the shop: Piedmont by Juniper Moon Farm! This sport weight yarn is 70% recycled cashmere / 30% recycled silk in 50 gram balls of 191yds / 175m.
Coming soon: new Fade Frenzy sets! Pulled from our stock of fingering weight hand dyed yarns, these collections of seven 25 gram mini skeins will be available in-store and on our website.

Tons of fresh house-dyed yarn is on the walls! We've got Sparkle DK, the return of 3-Ply Bulky, Sparkle Sock, and the brand new, ultra-luxe Yak Silk Sock.

✨️ Slide 1, Sparkle DK, L to R: 
Fanfic tropes: Mistaken Identity, Vampire AU, Fuck or Die, Huddling for Warmth, Fated Mates, Space Western, Miscommunication, Dream Talking, Enemies to Lovers, Wingfic

And congrats to our giveaway winner, yara 

Armando merch- totes, pins, and stickers- are available on our website and in our store.

Drool-worthy art by Stephen Draws 🕸️

On the rail, we've got a much-needed restock of 3-Ply Bulky, the ✨️new✨️ Yak Silk Sock, and everyone's fav, Irid Sparkle Sock. 
Which one is catching your eye?

We just received a restock of all your favorites from Amy Small 

#restock #lys #localyarnstore #handspun

recent_reviews.text: I was traveling and didn't bring a project. I stopped by, the person (sorry I didn't get your name) not only helped me choose yarn, he even printed out the pattern for me. recent_reviews.text:
Popped inside this cute yarn shop for the first time to get some clarity on a new project I wanted to start and hopefully purchase some yarn and needles. 

I unfortunately had the WORST customer service from the cashier which entirely turned me off from wanting to buy anything. It seemed as though my questions were bothering the cashier and I received a very hostile attitude from them overall in our conversation; to be frank, it left me wanting to run and hide (to preface--I have never ever felt this way before shopping in the city)! I ended up leaving that store feeling quite terrible about myself and pretty stupid for asking anything at all. 

While I thought that a neighborhood yarn shop would be the perfect place to get recommendations and advice as a newer knitter, this store is apparently not the place for that. It's a shame, too, since the products looked beautiful. Will probably not come back.
recent_reviews.author: Katarina ..

recent_reviews.text: Very helpful and friendly customer service.  Beautiful natural yarns, great selection as well as knitted and crocheted items for sale. Will come again!
recent_reviews.author: Susan B.

recent_reviews.text: This yarn store had a pretty wide variety of yarn and lots of great notions. One of the things I loved was their project bags; I got one with a picture of a chicken knitting on top of a pile of yarn. They had a couple different types of cascade yarn which is my go to. When I checked out,  the cashier went the extra mile and  double checked the dye lots and even went into the back to get yarn from the same dye lot. I cannot thank them enough!
recent_reviews.author: Julia L.

recent_reviews.text: Wonderful and very helpful people. Great choice of yarns and needles. Love all the local indie dyers yarns and the ability to use their ball winder
recent_reviews.author: Katrin V.

recent_reviews.text: Although I've made the odd (really odd) scarf, I consider myself a rank beginner. Nic was the epitome of a helpful/not condescending adviser. I'm definitely going to check out the twice-monthly Sunday office hours -- such a great idea for those questions YouTube just can't answer!
recent_reviews.author: Irene G.

recent_reviews.text: The employees here are so friendly and helpful. They assisted me in finding this gorgeous UV reactive yarn, and even suggested a skill level appropriate pattern for me to make with it. Five stars! Would visit again!
recent_reviews.author: Safire M.

reviews.text:
Awesome yarn shop, as unique as our city! Indie dyers, natural fibers, and A+ cheesecake pin up mascots! Their shop label yarns are small batch, gorgeous, and dyed by the owner.

(I'm disappointed by the amount of unkind reviews on here that compliment the yarn and then criticize the staff, who have never been anything but kind and helpful for the many years I've shopped here. Gotta assume it's user error.)

Really great yarn selection, very rude staff. Have been in a couple times where they’re dismissive and condescending, but this latest trip they were loudly celebrating that Petite Knit patterns aren’t in the top 20 patterns on Ravelry. It’s so wild to me how people love to put down others’ success. C’mon, move on, you have your own life and don’t need to loudly boast about patterns that are really helpful for beginners like myself. Let’s be adults!

Stopped in on a trip to SF and it was AMAZING! The young lady working there, Mural, was wildly helpful and so much fun to talk to. Wonderful selection of yarns and motions. Will absolutely be stopping by the next time I'm here. Highly recommend!

recent_reviews.title: Unexpected recurring membership
recent_reviews.text:
I discovered that I had been charged €40 on two consecutive months for a Change.org Membership that I do not recall intentionally subscribing to. I would never knowingly sign up for a €40-per-month recurring membership.

I searched my emails but could not find any membership confirmation, so the charges came as a complete surprise.

When I tried to contact Change.org through its online support form, it failed with a Salesforce error, making it impossible to submit my request.

I then contacted support by email. They cancelled the membership and initially refunded only the most recent €40 charge. After I wrote back requesting a refund of the first charge as well, they agreed to refund the remaining €40.

Although I appreciate that the matter was eventually resolved, I believe the membership sign-up process should be much clearer. A recurring payment of €40 per month is a significant commitment, and people should be fully aware that they are enrolling in an ongoing subscription.

My advice is simple: check your bank statements carefully. If you see a charge reading "CHANGE.ORG MEMBERSHIP", investigate it immediately to make sure it is a subscription you intended to take out.

Lindsey Isaacs spent 13 days in jail after investigators used data from a Flock automated license plate reader to find her SUV during an investigation into a crash that killed three people. But a 911 caller had described a maroon Dodge Durango and provided a partial license plate number that did not match hers. A later inspection found no crash damage to Isaacs’ vehicle.The charges were dropped, and another person was arrested.

This week, Isaacs shared her story before a U.S. Senate subcommittee examining Flock’s nationwide camera network. Her case comes amid a growing debate over how automated license plate reader data is collected and used. Flock says its camera accurately recorded Isaacs’ SUV and that the data should have been treated only as an investigative lead.

More than 65,000 people have signed a petition calling on lawmakers to ban ALPR surveillance systems nationwide, citing concerns about privacy, government overreach and potential misuse.

Read or sign the petition: https://c.org/TR6Ht9Xx

#Flock

For eight years, Albert Berto says he fed and cared for a colony of cats outside his Brooklyn home. Then, one morning, only one cat came when he shook their food can.

Berto said he found seven cats dead beneath his deck, several bleeding from their noses and mouths. He later reported that more cats were found over the following week, bringing the death toll to 18 cats. Three raccoons were also reported dead. Berto said he fed the cats, took them to the vet, and had them neutered and microchipped. The New York Post reported that a private veterinarian found high levels of rat poison in one cat recovered later that week. Official necropsy results for the first seven cats were still pending at the time of the report.

Berto and other neighbors told the Post they suspect a nearby resident may be responsible, citing the person’s past complaints about the cats. No suspect has been publicly identified.

A petition is demanding the NYPD and the ASPCA follow through on fully investigating and charging whoever did this.

A petition launched after the death of 15-year-old Daria Serkov is calling for additional youth bike-safety measures in New York City. Serkov was killed after a truck struck the electric Citi Bike she was riding with another teenage girl. Police said the truck and bike were turning right at the intersection. The 16-year-old operating the bike survived and was reported in stable condition. The crash remains under investigation.

Reports said neither teen was wearing a helmet. Under New York State law, bicycle riders under 14 must wear helmets; the requirement does not currently apply to all minors.

The petition calls on Citi Bike to use ID verification to prevent anyone under 18 from unlocking its bikes. Separately, it asks NYC officials to expand helmet requirements to all minors.

recent_reviews.title: Checkr is about to lose me the new job due to delays
recent_reviews.text:
In June of 2026 (less than 3 months prior to the writing of this review) Checkr completed a background check on me in under 2 minutes. About a week ago, a I received a once in a lifetime job offer. The only catch? Firm start date of 09/15/26.

No problem! I accepted, gave notice to my current employer, and immediately filled out the Checkr email from HR. The ETA was initially Fri 09/11/26. That got updated to 09/18/26. And now, on 09/13/26, I just received an email that the new ETA is... OCTOBER 26!

HR has already reached out to say they may have to rescind the offer because they cannot wait 6 weeks. Honestly, I don't blame them. I do blame Checkr.

Despite the recent check having cleared in 2 minutes, nothing in my life having changed since then, an absolutely squeaky clean record, and me having worked for many years in secure federal settings requiring MUCH more extensive background investigations than this, Checkr thinks a 6 week turnaround is appropriate.

Wildly unprofessional. I have tried to reach out the Checkr directly several times and simply get an automated chatbot. What a world we live in, where the fate of your family's well-being depends in part on a faceless company that can't be bothered to do their job, causing you to lose yours. Shame on Checkr. Shame.

FYI in case you are in a similar situation: The FCRA requires these companies to follow "reasonable procedures" in the procurement and assembly of background reports. California also has voluntary-assumption for forseeable negligence. As well as law on negligent interference with prospective economic advantage. Potentially negligent misrepresentation if you relied on the given ETA for other actions (such as resigning from your current job). I am not an attorney and this is not legal advice.

reviews.text: Como faco pra usar corretamente ?
جيد جداً

Very rarely will I take the time to write a review, as I tend to believe reviews can become more emotionally charged statements with a heavy bias only towards the squeaky wheels. As a result, I wanted to give myself some time to reflect and then share a professional and honest review in the hope that it can help other companies make a more informed decision.

There is a fundamental working challenge with this company which stems from their decision to move away from people-based accountability for supporting customer accounts. Like some other companies, ZenDesk moved solely to a ticketing based system where internal gig-style employees can pick up a ticket and help move things forward. Conceptually I can see where this could result in a 24 hour engine of support to ensure forward progress. However, the end result to the customer is that the lack of any individual accountability results in no one else having any empathy for the customer and seeing customer challenges from initial ticket through to completion. Team members are tagging other internal team members on the customer facing ticket to help each other understand what needs to be done to sign a contract. Our experience on our renewal has been one of the most embarrassing demonstrations of customer support for a company that is supposed to help you with customer support.

Because of the challenges in getting a consistent person to know what is going on and see what needs to be done to keep our account active, the account has "lapsed" twice, shutting down our customer ticketing and learning center requiring us to notify our end users on two different occasions. During each outage, the tickets are not met with any urgency or display of any empathy for this customer.

As the CEO of a health tech company, I hope that this experience is one that can help influence other decision makers when considering ZenDesk. I would strong recommend that you consider a different solution, one that prioritizes customers with a full team of responsibility and accountability with people owning the process for customer success and renewals.

recent_posts.text: For their exceptional contributions and hard work, we congratulate this year’s “Excellence … It Starts With Me” award winners, the Roy W. Simmons Community Service Award recipient, and the 363 employees celebrating years of service milestones.

Bob Wilson and Rick Wilson have joined Zions Wealth as senior vice presidents and wealth professionals and will be supported by client account service associates Jannet Sheehan and Heather Sullivan.

The team is based at Zions Bank’s Idaho headquarters at Eighth and Main in downtown Boise and will serve clients in Western and North Idaho and the Wood River Valley.

Rick and Bob, who are twin brothers, bring more than 30 years of experience in the financial services industry to the positions, most recently as wealth advisors and market managers at ICCU. 

As certified Chartered Retirement Planning Counselors, they specialize in building relationships with high-net-worth and ultra-high-net-worth individuals, families and business owners, and have extensive experience serving complex client needs through a disciplined approach to wealth management practices.

Investment Products: Not FDIC Insured | No Bank Guarantee | May Lose Value

We’re proud of Catherine Arik, Eastern Idaho/Wyoming region president, who was honored as one of the Idaho Business Review’s “Women of the Year.”

She was recognized for helping to shape Idaho’s economic and community well-being through her outstanding leadership, mentoring efforts and community involvement.

As region president, she’s focused on building a strong, empowered team of employees to provide a positive experience for clients. Her commitment to supporting small businesses has contributed to Zions Bank’s ranking as the no. 1 7(a) SBA lender in Idaho in 2023, 2024 and 2025.

Arik is a board member for the Regional Economic Development for Eastern Idaho (REDI) and serves as a mentor for People Helping People, a nonprofit organization that works to help single mothers obtain financial self-sufficiency. 

Congratulations, Catherine, and thanks for all you do for our clients and communities!

It’s been 20 years since Eli Madrigal opened her first Rancho Markets grocery store with the help of an SBA loan from Zions Bank.

Today, the independently owned, Hispanic-focused grocery chain has nine locations across the Wasatch Front and a new Idaho store in development.

Read about Eli’s entrepreneurial insight and guidance for small business owners: https://www.zionsbank.com/personal/community/business-feed/small-business-success-rancho-markets/

The golden goose of finances may not be a goose at all… but rather, a grandparent. In honor of Grandparents Day, our bankers share generational money lessons that stuck with them. 

https://www.zionsbank.com/personal/community/personal-finance-feed/golden-financial-guidance-from-grandparents/

Now through Sept. 14, join us in commemorating the anniversary of 9/11 at the Bastian Agricultural Center in South Jordan. The event includes a free immersive museum, community resource fair, and Touch-a-Truck exhibit. Learn more at majorbrenttaylor.com.

Today we commemorated Patriot Day with a ruck/walk/run organized by our Military and Veterans Employee Forum to honor and remember those affected by the events of Sept. 11, 2001.

We’re grateful to our forum members and all participants for creating a meaningful opportunity to come together in reflection and unity. #NeverForget

recent_reviews.text: I have been a Zions bank customer for fifty years.  As I matured and my financial profile vastly improved, Zions set me up with a personal private banker to assist in my financial matters.  Over the last ten years my banker slowly became withdrawn and eventually retired.  Service went from dwindling to non-existent.  Instead of supplying me with another banker I had to find one myself after multiple calls and complaints. Since I initiated first contact with my supposed personal banker I have heard nothing but crickets.  Not one call during the pandemic, no initiated effort to help my small business obtain PPP relief, NOTHING.  I am so angry and disappointed that I have been compelled to provide my first Yelp review.  Shame on you Zions bank!  This is the service I receive after providing Zions with multiple millions of dollars worth of business over the years.  Do not fall for the television ads suggesting Zions put their customers first.  If this is the way they treat customers who were included in Zions President circle, how are they going to treat average Joe.  Obviously Zions has become to big for it's britches and forgot who keeps THEM in business.  Based on my experience over the last four years, I suggest that anyone requiring financial services should stay away from Zions and find a bank or credit union who will truly deliver personal service.

recent_reviews.title: Customer Service not a priority at Zions Bank
recent_reviews.text:
March 14, 2025 First, let me start by saying, I am a responsible adult, I don’t bounce checks, I pay all my bills on time, and save as much as humanly possible, so I’m a good customer to have, and I don’t gripe unless I have a problem that is valid and on-going that I want to warn others about.  So here goes. 
On March 11, 2025, it looked like my computer might have been breached.  As I do all my banking online, I called Zions Bank and put a precautionary freeze on my  account.   Again, I put the precautionary freeze on my account.   I took my computer to Apple services that same day, they said that my computer was fine.  I called Zions back the following day, and told them to go ahead and take off the precautionary freeze.   They said that I’d have to come into a local branch.  I live 3 states away - it’s an online bank account.    As I did not have the time to argue with them, I called Zions again the beginning of April, I don’t remember the details of the conversation, but I assumed that the problem was solved - a simple freeze/unfreeze that I myself had placed.

In May, I get an automated phone call from my other main bank (not Zions) that there is an issue.  Long story short, my main back locks me out due a question about a transfer issue (I assumed that it was a deposit that I had made to Zions from my main account that didn’t go through due to the fact that, unbeknownst to me, Zions was STILL frozen), and the fact that I accidentally put in a wrong code once.   So now, my assets have been frozen for over 2 months at Zions, and I’m locked out of my main bank account.   Four days go by, no one at my main bank is getting back to me, and Zions is responding to my emails by saying that someone will get back to me - Just a loop of, “We’ll get back to you.”   So now, since these two banks are my main banks that carry my cash, I have no cash to pay my bills or grocery or whatever, and NO ONE is getting back to me.  My only option is to complain to an Ombudman, which will likely take months to resolve.

I’m disgusted.
 
Update: Zions bank just called me back for the first time in 4 days on my work phone (12:43pm) on my home/work phone not my cell.  They left no message, and if it were not for caller id, I would have never known who had called.   What good is a phone call without identifying who it is or leaving a message?       Now they can say that they couldn’t get a hold of me ….  More bad customer service.

recent_reviews.title: Charged An "Inactivity Fee" After 17 Years...
recent_reviews.text:
I opened a ZionsBank account in 2007. At the time the interest rates were "woo-hoo". As interest rates came back to earth, I eventually reduced my balance to $1.00. The bank dutifully sent me e-statements (~200 of them) over the years and an occasional inactivity form. At some point I stopped bothering to check the e-statements since they always showed my $1.00 was in "good-hands". Well yesterday, the bank sent me a "nasty letter" threatening to "throw me under the bus" with ChexSystems if I didn't pay the "huge sum" of $4.00. Apparently, the bank decided to start charging my $1.00 rent. I did call the bank's general customer service and the "collections" department to rescue my $1.00 to no avail. So now I'm sending four of its sibbilings ($4.00) off to ZionsBank Corp. To be sure I'm enclosing this less than glowing review with them.

Update: I few days later the bank sent another letter indicating that they charged "some accounts" inactivity fees "in error" a few months ago. They indicated that they are crediting the account (now closed) $5.09 (presumably $1.00 in the account and the $4.00 I sent them), plus 9¢ for my inconvenience. A check arrived for $5.09 a few days later. I couldn't make this up if I tried.

recent_tweets.text:
Quantitative survey analysis is on the verge of major disruption.

For the past 20+ years, advanced quantitative survey analysis has largely required specialized tools and expertise.

SPSS, R, Python, Stats iQ, External agencies.

For methods like MaxDiff, conjoint, pricing research, and other advanced analyses, there are still a lot of manual steps between asking a question and getting to a rigorous answer.

It's why we hear from so many research teams that they outsource their most advanced quantitative work to specialists.

AI opens up an entirely new frontier.

- What happens when the technical barriers to advanced quant start to disappear?
- How do we make these methods dramatically more accessible without sacrificing rigor?
- What should remain in the hands of an expert versus an AI?

I've been thinking a lot about these questions lately, and I'm spending the next few weeks talking with research and insights leaders who work deeply in quantitative survey analysis.

If that's you, I'd love to grab 20 minutes to compare notes on the biggest barriers today and what you think the next generation of quantitative analysis should look like.

Comment or DM me if you'd be up for chatting!

- Dozens of new capabilities for sophisticated survey research, including Conjoint and MaxDiff

Together with AI research agents embedded across the workflow, these capabilities help teams move from question to defensible insight faster without sacrificing rigor.
